data.body:
Lane-9119 re-check on origin/main 8e1be2da2a6 (arm64 macOS host, no Rosetta), before any edit:

- Confirmed prior comments: installed wheel tag `py3-none-macosx_11_0_arm64`; its `pypandoc/files/pandoc` is `Mach-O 64-bit executable x86_64`, sha256 d7b1e75c... = the pinned darwin-arm64 value. uv.lock lists both macOS 1.17 wheels (25553945 / 25553944 bytes).
- Fixture `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.json` records `generating_platform: darwin-arm64` with the x86_64 hash, so the frozen outputs were produced by the x86_64 pandoc 3.9 running on Apple silicon (Rosetta present on that host).
- NEW: on this host the provenance test SKIPS (`pypandoc.get_pandoc_path()` raises "No pandoc was found"; no PYPANDOC_PANDOC, nothing on PATH, no `~/.local/pandoc-3.9`). The 17 `Bad CPU type` failures in `make verify` come from the missing arm64 pandoc 3.9 prerequisite documented in docs/local-dev-env.md, not from this pin. Changing the pin alone does not make those 17 pass; installing the documented pandoc does, and that install then turns this ticket's provenance test red (the 18th).

Open: the design decision from the prior comment is still unmade, and checking byte-identity of arm64 output against the frozen x86_64 outputs requires downloading the upstream pandoc-3.9-arm64-macOS.zip, which needs operator approval. No claim, no code change made.
